title: What Is Black Friday? History, Origins & Fun Facts
description: Discover the origins of Black Friday, how it evolved into a global shopping phenomenon, and fascinating facts behind the post-Thanksgiving tradition.

sections.heading: What Is Black Friday?
paragraphs: Black Friday is widely recognized as the unofficial kickoff to the holiday shopping season. Taking place the day after Thanksgiving in the United States, it has traditionally been characterized by major retail discounts, early morning store openings, and massive crowds looking for holiday gifts.

Over the years, the concept has expanded far beyond traditional brick-and-mortar storefronts. With the rise of e-commerce, shopping events like Cyber Monday emerged, and Black Friday deals now frequently stretch across entire weekends or even weeks, transforming a single day of sales into a prolonged retail season.

sections.heading: The Surprising Origins of the Name
paragraphs: Long before it became synonymous with doorbuster sales, the term 'Black Friday' had entirely different connotations. In the 19th century, it was used in finance to describe a major stock market crash in 1869 caused by gold speculators.

The modern retail association began in Philadelphia during the 1960s. Local police officers used the term to describe the heavy, disruptive pedestrian and vehicular traffic that occurred the day after Thanksgiving as shoppers and football fans flooded the city. Retailers later attempted to rebrand the day positively, linking 'black' to the accounting term 'in the black,' meaning a business is operating at a profit rather than a loss.

sections.heading: How the Tradition Spread Globally
paragraphs: While deeply rooted in American culture due to its tie to Thanksgiving, Black Friday has grown into an international phenomenon. Countries around the world have adopted the shopping holiday, tailoring it to their own local retail landscapes.

In Canada, retailers eventually embraced Black Friday to curb cross-border shopping trips to the United States. Meanwhile, online retail giants helped popularize the concept in Europe, Australia, and parts of Latin America, where it now serves as a major annual economic event for both physical and digital stores.

sections.heading: Interesting Facts About Black Friday
paragraphs: One of the most notable shifts in Black Friday history is the transition from midnight openings to Thanksgiving evening hours, and eventually to online-first shopping. Many consumers now prefer browsing from home rather than waiting in lines overnight.

Electronics, home appliances, and toys historically rank among the most popular categories for deep discounts. Retailers often use these high-demand items to draw consumers in, while offering widespread promotions across almost every retail sector.

faq.a: Black Friday always falls on the day immediately following Thanksgiving in the United States, which is the fourth Thursday of November.

faq.q: Did Black Friday always mean shopping?
faq.a: No. The earliest documented uses of the term referred to financial panics or severe traffic congestion in police departments, long before it became associated with retail sales.

faq.q: Why do stores offer such large discounts?
faq.a: Retailers use steep discounts to attract high volumes of shoppers, clear out older inventory to make room for new merchandise, and generate excitement heading into the critical year-end holiday shopping period.
